text:
sara-security: Heads up — proposing we split the existing log.viewer into two roles: log.query (console/ES read-only) and log.export (can create exports/download). Exports MUST go through our masking pipeline and only write masked data to customer-facing buckets. Need feedback + migration plan by EOD :lock:

mike-eng-sre: Quick Q — what are retention boundaries here? SIEM wants 30d hot / 365d cold for alerts, legal asking for 7y for admin/audit events. Are we keeping exports beyond hot tier? :eyes:

olivia-privacy: Strong +1 for default masking on exports. Define protected fields: email, ip, user_id, full_name. Masking should be deterministic (so correlation works) but irreversible to plain text — HMAC with a KMS-wrapped key is our pattern. Also need consent check for customer PII exports.

alex-plat: Implementation sketch: export job writes raw to internal S3 (SSE-KMS, arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111222333444:alias/redwood-logs). A lambda batch job applies field-level masks using an HMAC key that's wrapped by the same KMS, then writes masked objects to the external/export bucket with presigned URLs for download. RBAC gate only lets log.export kick off the pipeline. Example proto config below.

sara-security: proto config (very rough):
```yaml
rbac:
  - name: log.query
    actions: [es:search, console:read_logs]
  - name: log.export
    actions: [export:create, export:download]
export_pipeline:
  input_bucket: s3://internal-logs/
  mask_job: lambda://log-mask-v1
  hmac_kms_key: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111222333444:alias/log-mask-hmac
  output_bucket: s3://customer-exports/
  presign_ttl: 1h
```

mike-eng-sre: For temporary access to the output objects, I'd recommend signed URLs + short TTL. For infra-side access (if a 3rd party needs access), use STS AssumeRole with session tags and an inline session policy limiting the object prefix and duration.

alex-plat: sample terraform snippet for role (very small):
```hcl
resource "aws_iam_role" "log_export_role" {
  name = "redwood-log-export-role"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.assume.json
}
resource "aws_iam_policy" "export_policy" {
  name = "log-export-policy"
  policy = jsonencode({
    Statement = [{ Action = ["s3:GetObject"], Resource = "arn:aws:s3:::customer-exports/*", Effect = "Allow" }]
  })
}
```

olivia-privacy: Two operational notes: 1) Audit trail must record who requested the export, which masking key id was used, and a fingerprint (HMAC) of raw records — raw records must NOT leave internal bucket. 2) Keep export request logs for 7 years (legal).

deploy-bot: New doc created: https://go/redwood/docs/log-export-masking-v1 :page_facing_up:

sara-security: Migration plan outline — canary in eng-sre: move a small set (~10) of existing log.viewer principals into log.query, run acceptance tests, then enable log.export as a JIT-granted role (1h TTL) for a week. After clean run, roll to prod and rotate the old role cleanup script to revoke the legacy log.viewer binding. Volunteers for canary?
mike-eng-sre: :raised_hand: I can run the canary and handle the acceptance tests (query latency, export pipeline success rate, masking verifications).
alex-plat: I'll prepare the terraform changes + a migration script to map existing log.viewer members into log.query or log.export based on current usage patterns. Will add a toggle in feature flags for rollout.
sara-security: Thanks — I'll draft the policy doc with explicit field list and retention table and tag owners. Posting an initial doc in #eng-security later today.
